messages:
tori: Heads up — after pushing the RAID controller firmware bump (LSI P2608 4.2.1 -> 4.2.3) on edge-usw2 rack rck-83, a subset of nodes' BMCs stopped answering quick IPMI queries. Fleet provisioner marked 7 GPUs unready and the scheduler started evicting pods. Observed ~09:12 PDT.

sam: Which hosts exactly? any common hw revision or BIOS microcode included in that package?

tori: Hosts: rck-83-12,14,17,19,21,23,27. Vendor bundle included a small BIOS/microcode update for the RAID controller. BMC logs show repeated timeouts: 'ipmi: rsp timeout' and 'oob: session reset'.

eli: Can you paste the ipmitool output/sol snippet you're seeing?

tori: ```
# ipmitool -H 10.40.83.12 -U root -P **** lan print
Error: Unable to establish IPMI v2 / RMCP+ session
# ipmitool -H 10.40.83.12 -U root -P **** chassis status
Error: Get Device ID failed
```

sam: tagging hw-eng and oncall for triage: @frank @anya :eyes:
oncall-bot: Paging eng-infra-oncall (severity: medium) — incident created 3777777779

frank: This pattern rings a bell — vendor microcode changed PCIe init sequence. On certain mobos the RAID init delays long and BMC watchdog fires during init, which makes IPMI unresponsive until the controller finishes. We saw a similar failure mode with P2608 on older backplanes. Workaround we used: temporarily disable BMC watchdog or increase the raid init delay in BIOS.

anya: Immediate mitigation needs to consider cost impact — provisioning backlog jumped, GPUs in 'pending' pool went from 18 -> 5 available in us-west-2. Autoscaler started spinning up nodes in other regions; cost estimate ~+$6k/day if we don't stabilize. Suggest draining affected hosts and spinning warm spare capacity in us-west-3.

sam: Can we hot-rollback the RAID fw remotely? Vendor tool 'percfirm' supports downgrade but it's invasive (requires controller reflash/reboot). I'd prefer canary rollback 2 hosts first.

tori: I'm setting maintenance now:
```
fleetctl set-maint rck-83-12 --reason "raid-fw-oob" --until "+30m"
fleetctl set-maint rck-83-14 --reason "raid-fw-oob" --until "+30m"
```
Starting rollback of rck-83-12,14 with vendor tool via jump host.

deploy-bot: rollback job started for hosts [rck-83-12, rck-83-14] (job id 5542)

eli: If rollback fails, fallback is BIOS knob to add PCIe init delay or disable raid controller in-board init and rely on OS-level driver init. Both have tradeoffs. Keep logs of BMC uptime counters.

frank: Also file to vendor: request patched image that preserves PCIe ordering or increases controller init window — we need a signed hotfix. Meanwhile, we should add a gating check in the firmware rollout pipeline to fail if BMC heartbeats drop during canary.

deploy-bot: rollback job 5542 completed: 2/2 succeeded.

tori: Rollback result: rck-83-12/14 back to 4.2.1, BMC responded in ~2m, nodes re-registered to fleet. Scheduler un-evicted 4 of 7 GPUs so far. Continuing to roll additional hosts in small batches.

anya: Good. Immediate action items: 1) drain remaining affected hosts, 2) spin up 10 warm spares in us-west-3, 3) pause any further RAID fw rollouts until vendor sign-off and runbook update. I'll open a cost alert and tag finance.

sam: I'll add a preflight check in the OTA pipeline that validates IPMI health for 10m after fw apply.

eli: Runbook note: add 'if ipmi session errors after raid fw, rollback to previous firmware; if rollback unavailable, apply BIOS PCIe init delay; escalate to vendor HW-eng'.

frank: Also add an inventory check to skip hosts with older backplane revision x3 (those were the ones that tripped last time).

tori: Thanks everyone — rolling in batches of 2, monitoring BMC+scheduler. Will update thread when all affected hosts are remediated. :thumbsup:

anya: Filing follow-up ticket for runbook + pipeline gating — FIN/OPS impact noted.

sam: Great triage, nice rollback.

(10:38 PDT) deploy-bot: all nodes in rck-83 stabilized, GPUs back to expected capacity.
